about: The pairing link from src/main/pairing.js: prefix + base64url without padding of the UTF-8 JSON object with exactly the keys v, id, n, a, p, k, t, x, in that order, written with no whitespace and no escapes (JSON.stringify). parseLink is strict: exactly one spelling of each link is accepted, the one encodeLink writes. Error codes name the first problem in check order: LINK_FORMAT, LINK_ENCODING, LINK_JSON, LINK_VERSION, LINK_FIELDS, LINK_ID, LINK_NAME, LINK_ADDRESS, LINK_PORT, LINK_KEY, LINK_TOKEN, LINK_EXPIRY, LINK_NONCANONICAL. a: 1-2 Tailscale addresses (isTailscaleAddress in addresses.json) in canonical text (dotted quad without leading zeros; RFC 5952 IPv6), at most one per family, IPv4 first. n: "" or lower-case DNS labels ([a-z0-9], inner "-", 1-63 each) joined by ".", at most 253 characters, no trailing dot. x is not compared with the clock here. Regenerate with node scripts/make-mobile-fixtures.js.

encodeLink.about: encodeLink(object) -> the link text. The object needs exactly the link keys (any order) and valid values; the same error codes as parseLink.

cases.note: the longest: 253-character name, both families, 64-character id, port 65535, x = 2^53 - 1
input key order does not matter; the output is canonical

parseLink.about: parseLink(text) -> {v, id, n, a, p, k, t, x}, or the error code of the first problem.
